subject: physics_2
question_text: Can there be electric potential at a point with zero electric intensity? Give an example.

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Two structural checks are IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the two-book union check (the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only) and the past-paper back-test (the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers). Hand-checked: E = −dV/dr, so a region of constant non-zero V has E = 0; inside a charged hollow spherical conductor V equals the surface value everywhere and E = 0 — the book's example is correct. The book prints 'Can there electric potential' (a dropped 'be'); the question text here restores it.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Yes, with the reason
lines: Yes. Electric intensity is the rate of change
If V has the same value at every nearby point,
E is zero even though V is not zero.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say yes AND give the reason E = −dV/dr.
steps.why: E measures how fast V changes from point to point, not how large V is. A region of constant V has zero slope, so E = 0 there while V keeps its value.
common_mistakes: Thinking zero E forces zero V. Zero E only forces CONSTANT V.

recall.must_convey: That yes, E is the rate of change of V, so constant non-zero V gives zero E.
accept: E is minus dV by dr
V need not be zero when E is zero

steps.memory_tip: E is the slope of V. A flat V, at any height, has zero slope.

steps.label: The example
lines: Example: inside a charged hollow spherical
equals the potential of the surface, and the
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name the hollow charged conductor and state both facts: V not zero, E zero.
steps.why: Inside a charged hollow conductor the charges sit on the surface and their fields cancel at every interior point, so E = 0; V stays at the surface value because no field means no change in V.
common_mistakes: Writing "inside a conductor" without saying charged and hollow.
Claiming V is also zero inside. V equals the surface potential.

recall.must_convey: That inside a charged hollow spherical conductor V is not zero but E is zero.
accept: V equals the surface potential inside

steps.memory_tip: Hollow sphere: the field stops at the surface, the potential walks in unchanged.

insider_note: The reason line E = −dV/dr carries the first mark; a bare yes with the example usually earns only one of the two.
